title: PicardExternalCoefficientsAffineLocalCohomology
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], X,Y schemes [def-pc-scheme], and f:X -> Spec(k), g:Y -> Spec(k) morphisms. Assume X is quasi-compact and the diagonal of f is affine. Let F,G be quasi-coherent modules on X,Y [pqf-def-coherent]. Put E=pr1^*F tensor pr2^*G [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. For every affine open V of Y and every q >= 0, there is an isomorphism of additive groups H^q(pr2^{-1}(V),E) [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] with H^q(X,F) tensor_k Gamma(V,G restricted to V). The first factor uses the scalarCohomology k-action induced by f; the second uses scalarObj for V -> Y -> Spec(k). There are no acyclicity hypotheses and no quasi-compactness or affine-diagonal hypothesis on Y.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, affine-open calculation and degree-zero direct-image formula; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BED

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of X supplies a finite set s of affine opens with supremum top. Use the subtype s as the finite index type. Apply the affine-diagonal criterion over top of Spec k to pairwise intersections and InfClosed.iInf_mem_of_nonempty to deduce affineness of every nonempty finite intersection. The finite family covers top by iSup_subtype.

Let A be the native Cech complex of F and R the exact restriction of scalars along scalarMap f top. For an injective resolution of F, affine acyclicity gives QuasiIso beta, while the covering property gives IsIso H(alpha). Compose H(beta), inverse H(alpha), inverse isoRightDerivedObj, then the exact scalar-restriction homology comparison, to obtain (R A).homology q isomorphic to scalarCohomology f F q.

Apply the affine Cech comparison for external coefficients to this finite family and V. It gives openModuleCohomology isomorphic to the underlying additive group of the homology of tensorRight(G(V)) applied termwise to R A. Every k-vector space is free and hence flat, so tensorRight preserves finite limits; tensorLeft is a left adjoint and tensorRight is naturally isomorphic to tensorLeft via braiding, giving finite colimits. ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso therefore identifies the homology of the tensor complex with the tensor of the homology. Tensor the factor comparison from step 2 and forget scalars. Compose these three genuine isomorphisms to obtain the original conclusion without changing its statement.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 33.29.1 (varieties-lemma-kunneth), affine-open paragraph and equality of Cech complexes after Let V be an affine open; checked online 2026-10-13

lean.statement:
theorem picardExternalCupCoefficients_affine_local_cohomology
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)]
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (((RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace q
        ((pullback.snd f g) ⁻¹ᵁ V)).obj (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)) ≅
        AddCommGrpCat.of (scalarCohomology f F q ⊗[k]
          scalarObj (V.ι ≫ g) (G.restrict V.ι) (Opposite.op ⊤)))
